```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = identical(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN"), "true") &&
    requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly = TRUE)
)
```

```{r setup}
library(nfldoinkeR)
library(dplyr)
```

The doinks table carries `nflverse_game_id`, and the kickers table carries
`gsis_id`. Those are the keys for joining to nflverse's schedule and player
tables. The nflverse tables come from nflreadr, which this package already
depends on.

## Doinks to games

```{r games}
doinks <- load_doinks()

schedules <- nflreadr::load_schedules() |>
  select(
    game_id,
    nflverse_game_type = game_type,
    nflverse_gameday = gameday
  )

joined <- doinks |>
  left_join(schedules, by = c(nflverse_game_id = "game_id"))

joined |>
  select(doink_id, season, nflverse_game_id, nflverse_game_type, nflverse_gameday) |>
  head()
```

Selecting and renaming the schedule columns before the join avoids name
clashes: both tables have columns such as `season`, `week` and the scores.

A left join keeps one row per doink only if the key is unique on the
nflverse side, which it is for `game_id`:

```{r rows}
nrow(joined) == nrow(doinks)
```

### Why `nflverse_game_id` is sometimes `NA`

```{r na-games}
doinks |>
  summarise(
    doinks = n(),
    keyed = sum(!is.na(nflverse_game_id)),
    before_1999 = sum(season < 1999),
    unkeyed_1999_on = sum(is.na(nflverse_game_id) & season >= 1999)
  )
```

There are two different reasons for an `NA`:

* **Before the 1999 season, always.** nflverse's schedule data has no rows
  before 1999, so there is nothing to look up. The package does not construct
  an id for those games, so these rows stay `NA` by design.
* **From 1999 on, a game that has not been matched yet.** The id is adopted
  from nflverse's own schedule file when OTU games are matched to it, not
  computed. `doink_release_info()$nflverse_join` gives the current counts of
  keyed and unkeyed doinks from 1999 on.

The data pipeline checks that every non-`NA` id exists in
`nflreadr::load_schedules()`, so a non-`NA` id that fails to join is worth
reporting.

## Kickers to players

```{r players}
kickers <- load_doink_kickers()

players <- nflreadr::load_players() |>
  select(
    gsis_id,
    nflverse_name = display_name,
    nflverse_position = position
  )

kickers_joined <- kickers |>
  left_join(players, by = "gsis_id")

nrow(kickers_joined) == nrow(kickers)
```

```{r na-players}
kickers |>
  summarise(
    kickers = n(),
    with_gsis_id = sum(!is.na(gsis_id)),
    without_gsis_id = sum(is.na(gsis_id))
  )
```

A kicker with no `gsis_id` could not be matched to an nflverse player, and
the join leaves the `nflverse_*` columns `NA` for that row. The kickers table
carries a `gsis_status_note` column alongside the id; counting it against
whether the id is present shows which notes go with which kickers:

```{r status-note}
kickers |>
  count(gsis_status_note, has_gsis_id = !is.na(gsis_id))
```

The data dictionary vignette lists the allowed values of `gsis_status_note`.
